messages:
maria-finance: Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands finance Q&A. A few people asked me to post the approval matrix + ticketing flow so we can close questions. Short version: approvals differ by amount + spend type. I'll lay out examples and ask leadership to confirm.

liam: Appreciate this, Maria. High level: headroom is healthy; we're not cutting product velocity but we need stricter gating on vendor spend >$25k and recurring services. Procurement's SLA for onboarding stays 10 business days unless it's critical.

maria-finance: clicking to add the matrix:
- <= $2k: manager approval in Confluence ticket -> auto-cc finance
- $2k-$25k: Finance + manager -> Procurement ticket required
- > $25k or new long-term contract: Finance + Legal + Exec approval -> Procurement RFP + executive signoff

sam-engineering: For infra credits or one-off cloud spend, do we treat as OPEX under $25k? Also, who owns the vendor security questionnaire step? (we hit this with the GPU reseller)

maria-finance: Good Q. Infra credits are OPEX; if under $25k normal flow applies. Security questionnaires: Procurement owns the intake, but EngSecurity will triage and usually takes 3-4 days.

ada-pm: How should teams request emergency purchases (e.g., urgent SLA to replace a key service)? Is there a fast-track path?

liam: Yes — emergency purchases: tag the Confluence ticket with "URGENT" and ping #eng-oncall + finance. For anything >$50k we'll still need exec phone approval but we can post-facto formalize paperwork within 48h. Keep emergencies rare.

jordan-product: For multi-quarter projects with mixed CAPEX/OPEX, who sets the budget owner and how do we track spend vs. gift credits (like promotional credits)?

maria-finance: Budget owners assigned at the project creation step in our budget tool (link: https://redwood.internal/budget). Promotional credits should be recorded in the same tracker as negative spend lines so cost forecasting accounts for them.

procure-bot: Procurement checklist updated: https://redwood.internal/procurement/checklist — includes security, SOW template, vendor onboarding ticket form.

sam-engineering: Will we get a template for procurement ticket that includes expected latency/cost estimate for infra vendors? That would help SRE reviews.

maria-finance: Yes, adding a field for "expected throughput/latency impact" and cost breakdown to the ticket template tomorrow.

liam: Thanks Maria. Action items: (1) update ticket template, (2) publish emergency purchase runbook, (3) procurement to document SLA exceptions for critical infra. We'll follow up in next week's ops sync.

maria-finance: I'll own 1+2. Procurement team — can you confirm SLA exceptions by EOD Friday? @procure-bot please nudge.

procure-bot: Noted. Procurement will confirm SLA exceptions by 2026-03-27. Link to draft runbook: https://redwood.internal/procurement/urgent-purchases-draft

maria-finance: Thanks all. If anyone has edge cases (consultants, GPUs, legal retainers), drop them here and I'll add to the matrix.

sam-engineering: adding GPU reseller edge-case now — they have a pre-paid contract last year, will DM details.

ada-pm: TY — this clarified a lot.

liam: Appreciate the prep. :thumbsup:

maria-finance: Closing loop — I'll post final matrix + template updates once procurement confirms.
